title: Father Tom, relatives and the St. James Parish musicians
summary: Breaux talks about his bartender father, a violin-playing grandfather, cousin Ruffin Walker's band in St. James Parish and the Claiborne Williams circle.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You're a little bit of a fella then.
Well, no, not then, because, I mean, I was born in 1960, and, uh, we moved from there when I was, before I knew myself. But, you probably knew my daddy, because my daddy used to be a bartender then.
He used to call him Tom.
That's right. His right name was Theo Field, but everybody that knew him called him Tom, bro. He used to work for the IC Railroad.
Did he play music at all?
No. No. I'm the only one of the family players that I know of other than Wellman.

And I understand my grandfather used to play. Theo, bro, from out of St. James Parish, but I never did know him. That was my daddy's daddy. I understand he played violin years back. And then, well, I had some other relatives. Ruffin Walker played for a while. That's a cousin of mine. He was a- Yeah, Ruffin Walker. Yeah, he was a trumpet player. He had his armband out there in St. James Parish, too. But he didn't play too long. He went into contracting business with Rick Masonry. And he did pretty well for himself, so he let music along.
Who did they play with out there? Did they play with any other bands other than their own?
Well, yeah. Well, that's where Claiborne Williams and all them fellas was from around that territory. Freddie Landry?

I didn't know him. Yeah, well, that's in St. James Parish. Yeah, St. James Parish. And they played off and on with him until Ruffin organized his own band. And then he had his band for a while. How long it lasts, I don't know, because I was not there. You see, all my people are from that territory.
How long did you stick with drums?
